product.summary: An online marketplace where construction companies rent heavy equipment from rental firms and pay through the platform.

source.quote: Rigshare is an online marketplace where construction companies rent heavy equipment (excavators, cranes, loaders) from rental firms.
We are three years old.

evidence.value: Revenue $1.4M a year, roughly doubled last year

source.quote: Annual revenue reached $1.4M and roughly doubled last year.
220 rental firms list about 1,900 machines
Rental firms list machines; contractors book them by the day or week and pay through the platform.
six backend developers (Python and Postgres)

external_systems.name: escrow service
external_systems.role: a licensed payment provider holds and pays out customers' money; bank details stay with it

source.quote: Payments run through an escrow service from a licensed payment provider.
220 rental firms list about 1,900 machines

observed.what: bookings, almost all in the Netherlands and Belgium

source.quote: about 3,100 bookings are made each month, almost all in the Netherlands and Belgium

projected.what: German bookings in the first year, the CEO's plan (the CTO expects fewer)

source.quote: the CEO's plan says 1,000 bookings a month in the first year, the CTO thinks less

peaks.what: share of the week's bookings made before noon on Monday

source.quote: about a quarter of the week's bookings come in before noon on Monday

availability.value: Must stay up, especially Monday mornings; slowdowns there lost two large rental firms this year

source.quote: Monday-morning slowdowns have cost us two large rental firms this year

data_categories.value: company names, contact people, phone numbers, booking histories

source.quote: We store company names, contact people, phone numbers and booking histories

source.why: Business contact details and booking histories; bank details stay with the payment provider.

sharing.value: payments through a licensed provider's escrow service; bank details stay with that provider

source.quote: bank details stay with the payment provider

jurisdictions_or_rules.value: customers almost all in the Netherlands and Belgium

source.quote: almost all in the Netherlands and Belgium

jurisdictions_or_rules.value: GDPR for EU customers; Germany adds no new rule as far as known

source.quote: Customers in the EU are covered by GDPR, and the German launch adds no new rule beyond that as far as our lawyers know.

requirements.value: never hold customers' money; payments only through the licensed provider's escrow

source.quote: we must not hold customers' money ourselves, because that would require a payment licence we do not have

source.quote: Payments run through an escrow service from a licensed payment provider.
Engineering is nine people

source.quote: six backend developers (Python and Postgres), two frontend developers and one engineer who handles infrastructure and on-call
On-call is a single person, which has become a worry.

build.value: engineering budget $1.2M this year, people included

source.quote: The engineering budget for this year is $1.2M, people included.
Hosting costs about $14,000 a month.

source.quote: we must not hold customers' money ourselves

goals.note: Launch in Germany before the June trade fair (CEO's ranking, which the board says counts)

source.quote: Launch in Germany before the June trade fair

goals.note: Keep the platform up, especially Monday mornings

source.quote: Keep the platform up, especially on Monday mornings.

goals.note: Hosting costs grow no faster than revenue

source.quote: Keep hosting costs from growing faster than revenue.

unknowns.question: Will the board keep the CEO's ranking, or put reliability first as the CTO asks?
unknowns.why_it_matters: The CTO wants three months of technical-debt work before any launch; the answer reorders the goals and the plan.

unknowns.question: Will Baumann Group sign, and when?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Baumann would need single sign-on and an API for its fleet system this year, and would add a large fleet.

unknowns.question: How many German bookings to expect in the first year?
unknowns.why_it_matters: The CEO's plan says 1,000 a month and the CTO expects fewer; it sizes capacity and cost.

unknowns.question: How fast must booking be on Monday mornings: is there a speed target the slowdowns broke?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Slowdowns at the Monday peak lost two large rental firms, but no target says how fast is fast enough; it sizes the peak capacity work.

unknowns.question: Which typeface should the booking pages use?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Typeface choice determines the visual style of the booking pages.

unknowns.question: How much booking data could be lost in a failure?
unknowns.why_it_matters: The provider holds money, not booking records. Lost bookings can invalidate rentals and payments; the answer changes backup durability.

unknowns.question: How long is customer data kept?
unknowns.why_it_matters: It sets deletion jobs, not the shape of the options.

unknowns.question: Has the platform faced any named attack or incident?
unknowns.why_it_matters: None is named; the slowdowns are a load problem.
